doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Recording the Mary Poppins album and the role of the bass
summary: His first album with Ellington was Mary Poppins, recorded in Chicago, and he discusses the bass foundation.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. A couple of the recordings that you did while you were with him, I was curious about, didn’t he do one, the music of Mary Poppins?
Yes. That was my first album.
Was that a decision by him to do that music or was that something that would have come from the record company?
Was it for Reprise? Or RC.
I think it was on Reprise.
Yeah that was the Frank Sinatra label, right? At that time.
Well he had to satisfy so many—

So many a year I suppose. Sure. So he did it in his way. And Billy says, “play this way,” I guess you call it a shake. Or he says, “ponticelli,” I’m not certain what the term is now I’d have to look it up it’s been so long. At the introduction.

And he says, “play it this way.” And that’s how that happened. And then there were other spots where he didn’t — he’d just have sketches or outlines of majors, sometimes he’d have a note here. So what you hear was the first album that I did. It was done in Chicago at Universal Studios. That kind of collaboration and Billy would tell me, he says — sometimes he’d play piano with us — and he says, “keep playing those low E’s. I want to hear that bottom.” And I had learned that the bottom. And I had learned that the bottom of the bass is where it is. After all, you are a bass player. In a group like that somebody has to play the foundation. And I notice that today a lot of cats are sort of like infatuated with the upper register. It sounds good. But somebody has to play the bass. Otherwise you have a group without a bass. And that’s an area that hasn’t been fully explored, that part of the instrument but that’s not the only part of the instrument. And there’s nothing like having — as a matter of fact it’s more difficult to play the lower notes than it is to play the higher notes. I mean to get a rich bottom, a nice, firm bass quality sound.
